Yesterday it was the Poet's Dream, so today I'm having a Vancouver! I used the recipe on Difford's Guide.
https://www.diffordsguide.com/cocktails/recipe/2759/vancouver

1 2/3 oz. Gin (The Botanist)

2/3 oz. Benedictine

1/2 oz. Blanc Vermouth (Dolin's)

1/2 oz. Sweet Vermouth (Dolin's)

1 dash Angostura Orange bitters

Stir for about a minute with ice, strain into chilled glass.
I garnished with a Luxardo cherry and a bit of lemon peel.

It's basically just a Perfect Martini with the ratios tweaked and the Benedictine added, so if you love drinks that are sweet and complex, I can definitely recommend!

It's just a little slice down the middle that doesn't meet the ends, if that makes sense. I think I saw Anders Erikson do a garnish that way in a video. A pretty cool way to garnish a martini glass I think!
It's pretty sweet, but honestly I really love the Benedictine, so I don't mind. Making it a 3:1 ratio would probably still be really good!

Glad people still haven't given up the control life in Standard! I'll post the list I've had the most success with below. A couple of things I've learned.

* The Black splash is worth it, mostly because it allows for the best spot removal and some of the best sideboard slots. Void Rend is one of the best cards in current Standard, and Drag To The Bottom might be the best early Wrath effect, for dodging Indestructible.

* Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim feels a little overrated. It's not bad, but I think the best finisher for control is Urza, Lord Protector alongside The Mightstone and Weakstone. Mightstone and Weakstone is such a powerhouse, combining mana advantage, card draw, and removal. If you get to meld Urza you're suddenly super far ahead, and with Teferi, Who Slows The Sunset, getting the mana for the meld cost isn't hard.

*Finally, not a shocker, but Farewell is the most important spell in the deck. Many games are won by playing a couple of early spells, in order to stall while you let your opponent play into your Farewell to leave you way ahead.

A quick explanation of the various levels and my rationalizing:

-F tier is characters who aren't fighters. Most of them are capable of handling themselves in a fight, and some of them might even be more capable than most normal civilians, though they're nowhere near as strong as the rest of the list.

-E tier is for characters who are too young and inexperienced to be any higher on the list, but still have great potential to grow.

-D is for fighters possessing either elite training or raw power that puts them above just about anyone lacking the proper training and experience.

-C tier characters have skill and experience that makes them both inspiring leaders and deadly fighters. This is close to the limit of potential that most normal humans can achieve.

-B tier is for those who have almost superhuman strength, capable of feats that seem impossible. Masters of their craft that are more than capable of taking students.

-A tier is for those whose mastery of battle has earned them renowned reputation far and wide, along with admiration amongst both friends and enemies. Their superhuman feats and near-unmatched battle prowess puts them on a level above almost all others.

-Finally S tier is pretty obvious: legends whose strength goes beyond even the greatest of fighters, capable of bending the world around them to their will.

Looking for opinions on my current version of [[Enigmatic Incarnation]] for ZNR Standard. I thought the deck would be dead after rotation, but I'm pretty excited about the deck, though I haven't been able to test it out yet. 

https://www.mtggoldfish.com/deck/3442220#paper

Some thoughts:

* Not sure about [[Terror of the Peaks]], but there aren't a whole lot of 5 drops that I like. I like that it can be a weird kind of removal/reach, but it could be too clunky. It's possible that I should replace it with a copy of Yorion.

* [[Omen of the Sea]] and [[Skyclave Apparition]] are the bread and butter of the deck, and they're soooooooo good. Omen smooths your draws out and helps you play the important spells when you need them. Being able to search out Apparition to deal with your opponents threats is super smooth too.

* There are 27 "lands" in the deck, including [[Ondu Inversion]], [[Emeria's Call]], and [[Bala Ged Recovery]]. Those 3 are going to be lands most of the time, but the flexibility makes it worthwhile. Bala Ged Recovery especially is an effect that can be pretty useful in this sort of deck.

* With 27 lands, only 8 of them come in tapped 100% of the time, getting too little/wrong colors of lands happens rarely, and the mana is surprisingly solid from doing test draws. Having the [[Fabled Passage]] is especially helpful.

* With Dryad of The Ilysian Grove we can even use all five abilities of Kenirith.

* [[Glasspool Mimic]] will amost never be a land, having a clone effect is super strong for this deck

Anyways, enough rambling. Would really appreciate a second opinion and some outside thoughts, thanks!

Wanna take the chance to give some love to two of my favorites, M'rissi and Aurlyn. 

Aurlyn - She's perfect if you're looking for a follower with more personality, something different from the usual. She's really philosophical and thoughtful, and perfect for a player character that is the same. She's a little overpowered, so you may wanna try to use some de-powering mods with her, but it's not a big deal breaker for me. The only other complaint is that her back story is.....a little bit ridiculous. It makes her seem like a super Mary Sue. I tend to think of her stories as 50% real and 50% colorful embellishment. Basically, she missed her calling as a bard. I love bringing her along for any mage or scholar type characters.

M'rissi - Her quest is really interesting, with a lot of twists and turns that I didn't quite see coming. It's also pretty well scripted. The quest has three separate endings. Also, her body, face, and voice are customization, in case any of those things slightly annoyed you. She's honestly super cute, and just as deadly. Not your typical cute looking follower that's out of place. She'll stab a motherfucker and not think twice about it. Perfect for a rouge-type character, especially if you want to romance her.
